question: What is the meaning of density in relation to physical properties?
description: Density is a physical property that describes the mass per unit volume of a material. It is an important aspect of materials and products, particularly in the context of sustainable construction and circular economy practices. Understanding density helps in optimizing material selection, processing, and assembly, as well as facilitating the separation, dismantling, and recycling of materials at the end of their life. In the context of the Material Property Ontology (MPO), density is specified as a property that can be associated with materials, such as crossbeam, and its value can be provided in units like 'g'. This information is crucial for designing and managing products and materials in a circular economy.

3.1.3
Composition properties
Figure 5 shows the composition property facet. This block of ontology helps to optimise
the selection, processing, and assembly of the constituent parts and materials of a product
and facilitates their separation, dismantling, and recycling at the end of life of a product
to maximise the circularity.
Figure 5: Composition property facet of the MPO.
CompositionProperty has two subclasses, ConstituentPart and ConstituentMaterial. For
example, crossbeam has constituent materials carbon fibre, glass fibre, epoxy resin, alu-
minium, foam, and film adhesive that have mass, and a source and destination in a circular
economy.
